direct_mechanisms: No direct PAX8 PMC-normalized mechanism paper was kept in pass 1; direct PAX8 stability and nuclear localization candidates remain mostly in PDF queue.
supporting_mechanisms: PAX3/PAX3-FOXO1 proteasome-dependent degradation by PROTAC, AKT phosphorylation, and Hsp90 inhibition; Pax3 monoubiquitination by Taf1; Pax7 NEDD4-mediated ubiquitin-proteasome turnover and CK2 phosphorylation-dependent stabilization; Pax5 acetylation/deacetylation and SUMO/deSUMOylation control of protein level; Pax6 acetylation-RNF8 ubiquitination-proteasome degradation; PAX2 hydroxylation; PAX-family domain stability and localization defects.
retained_keyword_families: PAX8 protein stability; Pax8 sumoylation; PAX8 nuclear localization; PAX family ubiquitination; proteasomal degradation; monoubiquitination; SUMOylation/deSUMOylation; phosphorylation-dependent stability; acetylation-dependent degradation; Hsp90 client; PROTAC
noise_keyword_families: PAX8-AS1 lncRNA; diagnostic marker/immunohistochemistry; PAX regulates downstream target stability; generic muscle atrophy proteolysis; generic kidney/thyroid/ovarian lineage expression; paired-box developmental genetics without protein-level mechanism
missing_keyword_families: SUMOylation; sumoylation; deSUMOylation; monoubiquitination; protein levels; functional domains; nuclear localization signal; paired domain stability; Hsp90 client; targeted degradation; PROTAC
recommended_query_changes: For pass 2, split direct PAX8 rescue queries for SUMO/sumoylation and nuclear-localization/domain language; exclude PAX8-AS1; require PAX-family comparator queries to include phrases such as protein levels, degradation, ubiquitination, SUMOylation, phosphorylation, Hsp90, PROTAC, or nuclear localization near the PAX term; avoid generic paired-box and broad expression terms.
recommended_abstract_rule_changes: Exclude PAX8-AS1 and expression/diagnostic-marker papers by default. Exclude papers where PAX regulates another target protein unless the paper also studies regulation of the PAX protein itself. Include comparator papers only when the PAX-family protein is modified, stabilized, destabilized, localized, retained, ubiquitinated, sumoylated, degraded, or directly targeted for degradation.
rationale: First pass found useful comparator mechanisms but direct PAX8 PMC evidence was sparse and key direct PAX8 candidates are not yet readable through PMC. Workflow policy requires using PMC learning to revise guidance and rerun before PDF intervention.
